item.title: ‘A relief that it was over’: China No. 1 Wei Yi on 'long break' after Candidates
item.description: In an exclusive interaction with TimesofIndia.com, China’s No. 1 Wei Yi opens up about the exhaustion of competing in his maiden Candidates Tournament, describing the end of the gruelling 14-round event as a relief. The Grandmaster reflects on his performance in Cyprus, the pressures of elite chess, why players sometimes need extended breaks to recover, and more.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Bill Gates' daughters join mother to sign as founding backers of $100 million fund
item.description: Melinda French Gates, alongside her daughters, has joined a groundbreaking philanthropic venture designed to enhance women's health globally. The Women's Health Co-Lab aims to generate $100 million, supporting diverse organizations over three years. Phoebe Gates highlights the ongoing challenges women encounter in health and safety. With over $70 million already pledged by prominent philanthropists, the initiative is actively seeking more funding to meet its goal and broaden its reach.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Pennsylvania woman’s $250,000 family farm sale remains blocked after sibling dispute
item.description: Siblings are embroiled in a legal conflict over the fate of their family-owned 60-acre farm in Pennsylvania. A sister residing on the land sought to sell it despite having a long-term tenancy. In response, her siblings filed an urgent petition to block the sale, citing property rights. The Pennsylvania Superior Court supported the injunction, illustrating the complicated nature of co-ownership and informal familial arrangements in property disputes.

item.title: Jailer 2 Day 2: Rajinikanth's film crosses Rs 200 cr worldwide
item.description: Rajinikanth's much-anticipated action flick, 'Jailer 2', starring Mohanlal and Vidya Balan, garnered massive success at the box office, raking in over Rs 200 crore within just 48 hours of its release. The film enjoyed robust performances both domestically and internationally, particularly in its Tamil version. Although there was a slight dip in earnings on the second day, audience turnout remained vibrant. Critics and viewers have delivered mixed reviews overall.

item.title: Court tells US to process Green Card applications for up to 55k people
item.description: A federal judge has ordered the reopening of the diversity visa lottery for 2027, allowing 55,000 applicants. The ruling came after a lawsuit filed against Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding the lottery's registration. Judge Jinsook Ohta mandated a 30-day registration period for submissions, which must meet eligibility requirements. Additionally, new policy changes require some applicants to return to their home countries for Green Card processing.

item.title: Ryan Clark challenges Stephen A. Smith over Lane Johnson’s retirement
item.description: Ryan Clark defended Lane Johnson after Stephen A. Smith questioned the Eagles tackle’s retirement and mental health reasons. Clark said the impact of someone’s words matters more than their intentions. Johnson retired on October 6 after 14 seasons with Philadelphia, explaining that his mental health and family priorities had changed and he needed to step away from football.

item.title: Russia building 'security zone' in Ukraine that won't be part of future peace talks: Putin
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the creation of a security zone within Ukraine to secure Russia's borders. He stated that his armed forces are successfully pushing Ukrainian troops beyond Russian territory. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov detailed that this buffer zone spans 660 km, with Russian control over 70 percent. The ongoing operation aims to ensure the necessary security for Russia, according to Peskov.

item.title: US temple plot, school shooting: Gun epidemic spares no one as debate goes off target
item.description: A neo-Nazi teen attempted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois, but his rifle jammed. The attack highlights ongoing debates about gun violence and societal issues, including parenting and mental health. Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi expressed horror that the attack targeted Indian Americans during worship. Many lawmakers condemned the incident, emphasizing the need to address religious and racial hatred in society.

item.title: Rs 10,000 crore for small businesses: Who can benefit from India's new SME Growth Fund?
item.description: The Union Cabinet has greenlit a substantial Rs 10,000-crore SME Growth Fund dedicated to bolstering small and medium enterprises. This initiative focuses on equity investments in growth-driven manufacturing businesses that demonstrate strong viability and scalability. While the fund's launch is promising, the specifics of how to apply are still under wraps, making its successful impact contingent on the effective expansion of the chosen enterprises.

item.title: Return of Gulf oil: Has Iran lost grip on Hormuz & what does it mean for India?
item.description: The US war with Iran exposed Tehran’s ability to disrupt the global economy by blocking the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, around 19 million barrels of crude oil were exported daily from the Middle East. However, September data from tanker-tracking firm Kpler showed oil flows recovering to an average of 16 million barrels per day, the highest since the conflict began.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: No Jadeja, Iyer to lead in last two ODIs: Check full Test and ODI squads vs NZ
item.description: The BCCI selection committee has announced India's ODI and Test squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. India will play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests on the tour. Fast bowlers Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj have returned to the Test squad. Shubman Gill will lead India in the first three ODIs, while Shreyas Iyer will captain the team in the last two matches.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Two vessels carrying 24 Indian seafarers hit by projectiles, drone in separate incidents
item.description: Union shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that two vessels carrying Indian seafarers were attacked in October. The MT ST 3 was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, while the YARA J was hit by a drone off Romania. Fortunately, all 24 Indian nationals aboard both vessels are reported safe and unharmed. India has condemned attacks on commercial vessels, citing concerns for the safety of seafarers.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: From Ronaldo to Ronaldinho: How 10 football stars earned UAE Golden Visas
item.description: From Cristiano Ronaldo and Paul Pogba to Rio Ferdinand and Patrice Evra, several football legends have secured UAE Golden Visas and built connections with the region beyond the pitch. item.title: TGIKS 5: Kapil Sharma jokes Saif Ali Khan has kids in every decade
item.description: Kareena Kapoor and Saif Ali Khan graced 'The Great Indian Kapil Show' with their lively presence. item.title: 'Got 9 people murdered': On cam, big claim by Nitish's MLA; then clarification
item.description: Recalling his sacrifices for Nitish Kumar, Anant Snigh claimed: “Who has made as many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then. He used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered,” Singh said. However, later the leader clarified that his remarks was misinterpreted and that he was referring to the killing of nine of his associates.

item.title: Curtains for Ravindra Jadeja in ODIs? All-rounder drops out of 2027 World Cup plans
item.description: Since the 2023 ODI World Cup, Ravindra Jadeja has featured in only 15 of the 32 ODIs India have played. In his last eight matches, he has picked up just three wickets at an economy rate of over six. Captain Shubman Gill has maintained that Jadeja was not dropped for the third ODI, but the 37-year-old is now fourth in the pecking order among India’s bowling all-rounders, behind Axar Patel, Washington Sundar and Harsh Dubey.
item.dc:creator: PRATYUSH RAJ

item.title: Why BCCI named two captains for India's New Zealand ODI series
item.description: India will have two captains during the five-match ODI series against New Zealand. Shubman Gill will lead the team in the first three matches, while Shreyas Iyer will take over for the final two games.

item.title: Oh(io) No: Vivek Ramaswamy's Catch-22 problem with MAGA
item.description: Ramaswamy is running to become Ohio governor, a position he perhaps sees as a stepping stone to something bigger in the party. Yet Ramaswamy’s association with Trump is increasingly becoming a liability among neutral voters, while his faith and skin colour are proving a deterrent among parts of the MAGA base.
